workflow.critical: Produce ALL 9 artifacts — no partial completion allowed
Every finding must cite specific file paths and line numbers
Load {techniques_csv} for analysis technique library (49 techniques, 10 categories)
Load {project_types_csv} for project type detection signals

step.goal: Scan workspace and detect project type
step.action: Scan the project root for: - Source code directories (src/, lib/, app/, etc.) - Configuration files (package.json, requirements.txt, Dockerfile, pom.xml, go.mod, Gemfile, etc.) - Documentation (README, docs/, wiki/) - Test directories (test/, tests/, __tests__/, spec/) - Build/deploy configuration (webpack, vite, Dockerfile, docker-compose, CI configs) - Database migrations (migrations/, db/, prisma/, alembic/)

Load {project_types_csv} and match detection signals against the workspace scan: - Check each project_type's detection_signals against found files and directories - A project can match MULTIPLE types (e.g., fullstack = frontend + backend) - Score each type by number of matching signals - Select the best-matching project type(s)

Determine project scale: - **Small** (< 50 source files): Quick depth is sufficient for most techniques - **Medium** (50-500 source files): Standard depth recommended - **Large** (500+ source files): Deep depth for critical areas, standard for others

step.goal: Select analysis techniques and present analysis plan
step.action: Load {techniques_csv} — the full library of 49 analysis techniques across 10 categories

Filter techniques by relevance: 1. Match techniques where project_types includes the detected project type (or "all") 2. Prioritize techniques from the priority_categories defined in {project_types_csv} for this project type 3. Filter by depth: include techniques where depth <= recommended_depth (quick ⊂ standard ⊂ deep) 4. Result: a ranked list of applicable techniques, grouped by which artifact they feed into
Present the analysis plan to the user:
WAIT for user to confirm or adjust the plan

check.action: Update the technique list based on user preferences
Filter techniques to only those feeding the selected artifacts
Mark unselected artifacts as "skipped" (will not be generated)

step.action: Apply the following techniques from the approved plan that feed into business-overview: - Input-to-Output Tracing (if selected): trace critical user flows - Any other techniques targeting this artifact

Analyze README, docs, comments, and code structure to determine: - Business domain and purpose - Key user workflows - Business rules embedded in code - Domain terminology (ubiquitous language) - Business value and target users
Write to: {re_output}/business-overview.md
At the end of the artifact, include a "Techniques Applied" section listing which techniques from the CSV were used

Apply approved techniques that feed into architecture: - Layer Detection Analysis: identify architectural layers - Module Boundary Mapping: map coupling and cohesion - Dependency Graph Construction: build import graph as Mermaid diagram - Design Pattern Recognition (if deep): identify patterns and anti-patterns - Entry Point Discovery: find all entry points - State Management Mapping (if frontend/fullstack): map state stores - Event Flow Analysis: map event-driven patterns - Data Transformation Chain (if deep): trace data through middleware - Schema Extraction (if data_layer techniques selected): produce ER diagram - Relationship Mapping: map entity relationships - Any other approved techniques targeting this artifact
Produce Mermaid diagrams for: - High-level system architecture - Module dependency graph - Data flow diagram - Entity-relationship diagram (if applicable)
Write to: {re_output}/architecture.md
Include "Techniques Applied" section

Apply approved techniques that feed into code-structure: - Dead Code Detection: find unused exports and orphaned files - Naming Convention Audit: check consistency of naming patterns - Environment Variable Mapping: map all env var references - Any other approved techniques targeting this artifact

Map the complete codebase structure: - Directory tree with descriptions - File organization patterns - Naming conventions (document dominant patterns) - Module/package boundaries - Entry points (main files, route registrations) - Shared utilities and helpers - Dead code areas flagged for cleanup
Write to: {re_output}/code-structure.md
Include "Techniques Applied" section

Apply approved techniques that feed into api-documentation: - Route Registration Scan: find all HTTP routes - Middleware Chain Mapping: map middleware execution order - Auth Flow Tracing: trace auth lifecycle - API Contract Extraction: extract request/response schemas - API Versioning Detection (if deep): check versioning strategy - Webhook Detection: find webhook handlers - Any other approved techniques targeting this artifact

Discover and document all APIs: - REST endpoints (method, path, params, response) - GraphQL schemas and resolvers - gRPC service definitions - WebSocket events - Internal service APIs - Authentication/authorization requirements per endpoint - Middleware chain per route
Write to: {re_output}/api-documentation.md
Include "Techniques Applied" section

Apply approved techniques that feed into component-inventory: - React Component Tree Analysis (if React): map hierarchy, prop drilling, context - Spring Bean Analysis (if Spring): map DI graph - Next/Nuxt SSR Analysis (if Next/Nuxt): analyze server/client boundary - Mobile Navigation Flow (if mobile): map screen navigation - Schema Extraction: extract DB entity inventory - Message Queue Analysis (if deep + microservices): map producers/consumers - Any other approved techniques targeting this artifact

Catalog all significant components: - Classes/modules with responsibilities - UI components (if applicable) with hierarchy - Services and their interfaces - Middleware and interceptors - Database models/entities - Event handlers and listeners - Relationships and dependencies between components
Write to: {re_output}/component-inventory.md
Include "Techniques Applied" section

Apply approved techniques that feed into technology-stack: - CI/CD Pipeline Analysis: analyze build/test/deploy - Container Configuration Review: analyze Docker/k8s configs - Build System Analysis: analyze bundler/transpiler/package manager - Bundle Size Analysis (if frontend): analyze JS/CSS bundles - Environment Variable Mapping: catalog all env vars - Any other approved techniques targeting this artifact

Identify the complete technology stack: - Languages and versions - Frameworks and versions - Build tools and configuration - Database systems - Cache systems - Message queues - Cloud services / infrastructure - CI/CD pipeline configuration - Development tools (linters, formatters, etc.)
Write to: {re_output}/technology-stack.md
Include "Techniques Applied" section

Apply approved techniques that feed into dependencies: - Dependency Vulnerability Check: cross-reference against CVE databases - External API Dependency Mapping: catalog outbound service calls - Third-Party SDK Inventory: catalog integrated SDKs - Any other approved techniques targeting this artifact

Analyze all external dependencies: - Direct dependencies with versions - Transitive dependency tree (high level) - License analysis - Known vulnerabilities (flag outdated/CVE-affected packages) - Dependency categorization (runtime, dev, peer) - Heavy dependencies (large packages that could be replaced) - External service dependencies (APIs, SDKs)
Write to: {re_output}/dependencies.md
Include "Techniques Applied" section

Apply approved techniques that feed into code-quality-assessment: - OWASP Top 10 Quick Scan: check for common vulnerabilities - Auth Pattern Analysis (if deep): deep auth security check - Input Validation Audit: check sanitization patterns - Secret Detection Scan: find hardcoded secrets - Dead Code Detection: find unused code - Code Duplication Analysis: identify copy-paste patterns - Complexity Metrics Scan: measure cyclomatic complexity - Test Coverage Mapping: map tested vs. untested code - ORM Pattern Detection (if data_layer): find N+1 queries - N+1 Query Detection: scan for loop-based queries - Caching Pattern Review (if deep): identify caching gaps - Async Flow Analysis: check error handling in async code - Memory Leak Risk Detection (if deep): find leak patterns - Error Propagation Tracing: trace error handling layers - Any other approved techniques targeting this artifact

Assess code quality across dimensions: - **Security:** OWASP findings, auth issues, input validation, secrets - **Reliability:** error handling, async patterns, test coverage - **Maintainability:** complexity, duplication, naming, dead code - **Performance:** N+1 queries, caching gaps, bundle size, memory risks - **Accessibility:** compliance (if UI)
For each finding, provide: - Severity: Critical / High / Medium / Low - File and line number - Description of the issue - Recommended fix
Write to: {re_output}/code-quality-assessment.md
Include "Techniques Applied" section
After all artifacts are generated, present enhancement options:
WAIT for user choice

check.action: Show available deep techniques not yet applied for that artifact from {techniques_csv}
Apply selected techniques and update the artifact
Re-offer enhancement options (loop back to this step)

Compare findings across artifacts: - Does the architecture description match the actual code structure? - Do API docs match the route registrations found in code-structure? - Do component relationships match the dependency graph? - Do security findings align with the dependency vulnerability report?
Flag inconsistencies and update affected artifacts
Re-offer enhancement options (loop back to this step)
List remaining techniques not yet applied
Apply them to the relevant artifacts
Re-offer enhancement options (loop back to this step)

step.action: Create executive summary: - One-paragraph project description - Key findings (top 5, ranked by impact) - Risk areas (ranked by severity) - Recommended improvements (prioritized) - Confidence scores per artifact (High/Medium/Low) with justification - Analysis metadata: - Project type detected - Depth level used - Techniques applied (count and list) - Techniques skipped (and why) - Total analysis time
Write to: {re_output}/reverse-engineering-summary.md
Log completion to audit trail
